method.gate_rule: For each T in {2018, 2022}, estimate house effects from last polls in cycles with election year < T, using partial pooling toward zero with prior_strength=3.0. In cycle T, the unadjusted forecast is the equal-weight mean of last polls. The adjusted forecast subtracts the shrunk house effect (zero if the institute is unseen). The score is the L1 distance to the official national result. SUPPORTED only if the adjusted forecast has strictly smaller L1 in both 2018 and 2022. The rule is not changed after seeing the scores.

audit.recommendation: Level C must not be production input. More than half of the sampled rows could not be confirmed. Several Wikipedia hrefs point to the wrong year. Restrict C, especially 2014, before house effects are allowed to move a live forecast.

error_components.small_sample_caveat: The common component is estimated from 6 cycle-mean residual vectors with a Bessel correction (divide by C-1) and with the expected noise of those means subtracted. Six cycles is a small sample; the common variance is noisy.

intervals_2026_overlay.defensible_reason: The naive overlay adds last-poll residuals on top of Dirichlet sampling error and treats a five-institute average as if it were one poll. The decomposed overlay keeps the common election-day miss and the institute component divided by Kish n_eff, and it leaves sampling error to Dirichlet.

probabilities_2026.interpretation: The official set answers how much the five current polls disagree. Only the decomposed set is a probability about the election result, and it still omits late opinion movement and turnout uncertainty.
